notes.content: This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details. TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx FINANCIAL AID Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs) A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units. EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration TEST CREDIT If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit TRANSFER HELP Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors! Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4 Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar , on the first floor of University Hall ( interactive map link ).
notes.contentHtml:
This agreement displays only the lower-division courses required in the major. Although completion of the coursework listed below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower-division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, general education, or all-university requirements necessary for completion of this degree. In some cases, there may be alternative course options at the upper-division level. Please review the CSUSB catalog for full details.


TRANSFER ADMISSION INFORMATION

You can find information about admission to CSUSB as a transfer student here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students


TRANSFER SUCCESS PATHWAY

Enrolling in the Transfer Success Pathway provides you with dual admission to a California Community College and a specific CSU campus. The TSP ensures a more streamlined transfer experience since you can choose the specific community college courses that will apply to your intended major at your destination CSU campus. See if you qualify for the Transfer Success Pathway here: https://www.calstate.edu/apply/transfer/Pages/transfer-success-pathway.aspx


FINANCIAL AID

Students who plan to transfer directly from a California Community College to a 4-year university can apply for the Cal Grant Transfer Entitlement Award. The application deadline is March 2nd each year, and students must submit a FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application. The minimum GPA is a 2.40. More information is available here: https://www.csac.ca.gov/post/cal-grant-transfer-entitlement-award


ASSOCIATE DEGREES FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

A complete list of CSUSB majors/concentrations that are similar to the Associate Degrees for Transfer (ADTs) can be found here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/associate-degree-transfer

Students who intend to transfer to CSUSB with the ADT guarantee MUST submit final transcripts with the earned ADT recorded by the final document deadline: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-deadlines

Students who submit transcripts after the document deadline are NOT guaranteed to graduate within 60 semester units.


EXPLORE MAJORS AND CAREERS

  • The CSUSB Career Center has collected a variety of resources to help students choose or confirm their major and explore different career paths: https://www.csusb.edu/career-center/students/career-resources/major-and-career-exploration


TEST CREDIT

If you took an AP, IB, or CLEP test, you can look up your CSUSB credit here: https://www.csusb.edu/registrar/articulation/test-credit


TRANSFER HELP

Do you have questions about your transfer work? Need some guidance? You can talk with one of our Transfer and Graduation Counselors!

  • Email: transferhelp@csusb.edu
  • Phone: 909-537-5200, Option 4
  • Zoom: Set up an appointment by emailing transferhelp@csusb.edu

You are also welcome to visit us in person. We are located in the Office of the Registrar, on the first floor of University Hall (interactive map link).

notes.content: The requirements below are for the pre-licensure program in Nursing. Students who have already completed an A.S. in Nursing and hold an active California RN license (or are in-progress with either) should refer to the RN to BSN Bridge Program . ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS Admission is selective. Meeting minimum prerequisites does not guarantee admission to the program. Acceptance into CSUSB as a Pre-nursing student; Completed pre-licensure BSN program application, submitted by applicable published deadline; Completion of the ATI Test of Essential Academic Skills (TEAS) pre-admission examination, with a score of at least 70, by admission application deadline; An overall cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 3.5 or better; A GPA of 3.0 or better on completed required prerequisite courses (all prerequisite courses listed below); A grade of C (2.0) or better in each prerequisite course; Attendance at a CSUSB Nursing Information Session; California Residency per requirements for admission to CSU Impacted Programs; Additional consideration and preference is given to: Residents of the CSUSB local area. Applicants who are bilingual. Nursing is an impacted major at CSUSB. Impaction information for applicants is available here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-impaction-criteria MAJOR INFORMATION Students in the Nursing major must earn grades of "C" or better in all nursing prerequisite courses, corequisite courses, and courses in the nursing major. If a grade less than C (2.0) is earned in any nursing major course, the student will be dismissed from the Nursing program. Dismissed students may request readmission after failure of a nursing course one time. If readmission is approved, the student may re-take the failed course and take all remaining nursing courses a maximum of one time on a space-available basis. notes.contentHtml:
The requirements below are for the pre-licensure program in Nursing.

Students who have already completed an A.S. in Nursing and hold an active California RN license (or are in-progress with either) should refer to the RN to BSN Bridge Program.


ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Admission is selective. Meeting minimum prerequisites does not guarantee admission to the program.

  1. Acceptance into CSUSB as a Pre-nursing student;
  2. Completed pre-licensure BSN program application, submitted by applicable published deadline;
  3. Completion of the ATI Test of Essential Academic Skills (TEAS) pre-admission examination, with a score of at least 70, by admission application deadline;
  4. An overall cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 3.5 or better;
  5. A GPA of 3.0 or better on completed required prerequisite courses (all prerequisite courses listed below);
  6. A grade of C (2.0) or better in each prerequisite course;
  7. Attendance at a CSUSB Nursing Information Session;
  8. California Residency per requirements for admission to CSU Impacted Programs;


Additional consideration and preference is given to:

  1. Residents of the CSUSB local area.
  2. Applicants who are bilingual.


Nursing is an impacted major at CSUSB. Impaction information for applicants is available here: https://www.csusb.edu/admissions/apply-csusb/transfer-students/transfer-impaction-criteria


MAJOR INFORMATION

Students in the Nursing major must earn grades of "C" or better in all nursing prerequisite courses, corequisite courses, and courses in the nursing major. If a grade less than C (2.0) is earned in any nursing major course, the student will be dismissed from the Nursing program. Dismissed students may request readmission after failure of a nursing course one time. If readmission is approved, the student may re-take the failed course and take all remaining nursing courses a maximum of one time on a space-available basis.


ALL MAJOR REQUIREMENTS

The complete list of major requirements is available here: http://bulletin.csusb.edu/colleges-schools-departments/natural-sciences/nursing/nursing-bs/


ARTICULATION AGREEMENT NOTES

Articulates as a Series Only: If this description appears next to a requirement below, please refer to the Department Articulation Agreement for that course for more information. It typically means that an exact articulation to the CSUSB requirement is not possible.


CSUSB ADVISING PODCASTS

Find out more about this major here:

  • What is the Nursing Major?


ASSOCIATE DEGREE FOR TRANSFER (ADTs)

This major does not have a corresponding Associate Degree for Transfer (ADT).
